name: Windows 365 for Agents

modes.label: Pay-as-you-go Cloud PC for Agents (US geography)

sizes.name: Cloud PC for Agents (hardware spec not published)

modes.note: "For US Geography, the Windows 365 for Agents Cloud PCs are billed at $0.40 per hour for consumption. Usage is calculated as the total time spent running agent tasks on provisioned Cloud PCs within each hourly window, rounded up to the next full hour." Always-available Cloud PCs are the same Cloud PC and the same $0.40/h usage plus "$5 per Cloud PC per month ... in addition to any Pay-as-you-go based usage" (merged here; the $5 add-on is not in the mode maths). Windows licence included. Sessions have no fixed maximum duration while the agent sends an MCP request at least every 30 minutes; after 30 minutes without MCP activity the session is evicted, the Cloud PC resets, and capacity returns to the pool.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go (Microsoft tenant)
plans.note: Driven through Copilot Studio computer use, Project Opal, Researcher or Agent 365; provisioning policies / agent pools in Intune. Any prerequisite Copilot Studio / Agent 365 licences are not included here.

caveats: Cloud PC vCPU/RAM/disk not published (sizes vcpu/ram null): the engine cannot size-match; treat as one Cloud PC per agent session at $0.40/h.
Only the US price is published; "Pricing varies based on the geography where Cloud PCs are provisioned."
Rounding is per hourly window: a 10-minute task bills a full hour; tasks straddling a window boundary can bill 2 hours.

Always-available option (formerly a separate regime, merged 2026-09-28): same $0.40/h usage plus a fixed $5 per Cloud PC per month for instant availability (interactive / Agent 365). Add $5 x always-available PCs to the monthly total; not captured by the mode maths.
Microsoft-stack only: agents run through Copilot Studio / Project Opal / Researcher / Agent 365 and Intune; not a generic VM or sandbox API. Prerequisite product licences are not included.
Storage, egress, IPv4: none published / not applicable (null).

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.notes: Agent pools are sized by a Cloud PC count; active plus available sessions equals the provisioning policy's always-available Cloud PC count. Public default and maximum counts were not found.

snapshot_auto.quote: Checkpoint state externally. In-session state does not survive an unexpected session loss. If the session is interrupted, the Cloud PC resets on release and any unsaved work inside the session is lost.
snapshot_auto.note: Cloud PCs for Agents are stateless: reset to the provisioned image after every session (checkin, policy termination or 30-min idle eviction). Nothing is saved.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Cloud PCs are stateless and reset after every agent session, which ensures that no credentials persist and no trust carries across workloads.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint API in the Session API, MCP tools or Graph pool APIs; docs tell you to save progress to external storage. Pools boot from gallery or uploaded custom images (admin-side image, not a session snapshot).

harness_api.quote: Agentic app: A host that contains a model and an orchestrator. The orchestrator calls Computer-Get to claim a Cloud PC and Computer-Do to operate it.
harness_api.note: The agent (Copilot Studio, Project Opal, Researcher, Manus, your own) runs outside; the Cloud PC is driven via a per-session MCP endpoint (mouse/keyboard/screenshot, command execution, browser automation). That is a computer-use/exec surface, not an API to drive a harness inside the PC.

egress_allowlist.quote: GSA monitors and enforces policy across all outbound traffic from the Cloud PC. The internet traffic flows through the internet access profile. This approach allows organizations to apply web content filtering, URL-based controls, and threat protection policies inline
egress_allowlist.note: Via Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access (Entra Internet Access, separately licensed): FQDN / URL / web-category allow/block, enforced in Microsoft's Security Service Edge, but traffic capture depends on the GSA client deployed into the Cloud PC via Intune. No native per-pool network allowlist in W365A itself.

egress_http_rules.quote: HTTP method request filtering: Block or allow specific HTTP methods, such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE.
egress_http_rules.note: Entra Internet Access web content filtering (used by W365A via GSA) also supports URL filtering and an agent-vs-user source traffic type condition. Separate Microsoft product/licence; client-based traffic capture.

guest_firewall.quote: This security Baseline includes Microsoft-recommended settings across several security categories such as Microsoft Defender Antivirus, Microsoft Defender Firewall, Attack Surface Reduction (ASR), credential protection, browser security, and operating system hardening.
guest_firewall.note: Windows 11 Cloud PC (full VM); host firewall is Windows Defender Firewall (not nftables/iptables), configured by admins through Intune policy. Whether the agent user has local admin is not documented.
